claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug ...
claims.source_checked: doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru (DNS refused by session network policy; not read); doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z -> nature.com / idp.nature.com (proxy 403 / DNS refused; not read)
claims.note: Kola SG-3 at 12,262 m as the deepest point ever reached by drilling rests on Lobanov 2021 and Zhu & Huang 2026, neither of which could be opened. A4: the hook also implies it is still the deepest as of 2026 (needs a source dated near now; Zhu & Huang 2026 would do if it says so) and says 'dug' for a drilled borehole (framing a pedant may flag; harmless). The SOURCES block's deepest-vs-longest distinction is right in principle but was not checked against a source.

claims.claim: ... is narrower than a dinner plate.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/S0040-1951(99)00065-7 -> linkinghub.elsevier.com (proxy 403; not read); doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru (DNS refused by session network policy; not read); SOURCES entry 2 read
claims.note: The script's own SOURCES entry 2 says the 214 mm figure is the bit and the open hole below the casing, that the top is cased at 245 mm to 8,278 m (a casing sits in a hole drilled wider than itself), and that below 7 km 'the bore went oval with caverns', '21 cm is the drilled width, not a constant'. So a flat statement about the hole's width overstates what its own record supports (A3), and a viewer who swipes at second two leaves with that statement (A4). Change to a claim the record supports, e.g. 'was drilled with a bit narrower than a dinner plate' or 'For most of its depth, the deepest hole ... is narrower than a dinner plate', and confirm 214 mm against Popov 1999 / Lobanov 2021 (not reachable here).
